thread:
maria: Heads up: we have a latency spike in ap-south2 for generation routes, started ~1978123000. 95th jumped from ~120ms to ~820ms.
kevin: Confirming. Dashboards show batch sizes collapsing and a surge in KV-cache misses. I can tail logs.
kevin: `grep -i \"kvcache miss\" /var/log/runtime/* | tail -n 50` output shows repeated miss/evict loops.
kevin: sample:
```
2026-03-18T10:02:13Z runtime INFO kvcache: miss key=user-ctx-...
2026-03-18T10:02:13Z runtime WARN batcher: dispatch size=1
2026-03-18T10:02:13Z runtime INFO kvcache: evict key=user-ctx-...
```
nora: That looks like the kvcache eviction hot-loop we've seen before. Did the runtime bump land last night?
maria: Yes, runtime v1.9.7 rolled at 1978121200 with batching tweaks.
devon: I see an increase in small request fanout from the APAC promo traffic, TTLs are short, so prefix caching isn't helping.
ops-bot: @channel Incident created: INC-APAC-KVCACHE-1978123456. Priority: P1.
kevin: Mitigation options: 1) force traffic shift away from ap-south2 to na-west/na1 pools, 2) emergency revert to v1.9.6, 3) tweak runtime config to serialize batching and increase kvcache TTL.
maria: Quick cost note: shifting traffic to NA will increase egress and spot GPU consumption; we need approval to scale dedicated pools for a few hours.
sre-oncall: Approve temporary capacity spend up to $6k for the next 6 hours if it avoids SLA misses.
kevin: I'm going to try a non-invasive config change first: bump kvcache TTL for generation routes and cap `max_batch_bytes` to force more predictable batching. Pushing via config service now.
kevin: command: `curl -XPOST https://config.internal/api/set -d '{\"runtime.kvcache.ttl_ms\":60000,\"batcher.max_batch_bytes\":262144}'`
deploy-bot: config-change accepted: change_id=cfg-1978123456-1 rolling to ap-south2 (5 nodes at a time).
maria: After first roll we see 95th drop from 820ms -> 420ms but still above baseline. KV miss rate down ~35%.
devon: Good. Preparing a rollback plan and a runtime hotfix (kvcache lock ordering + guard) as branch hotfix/kvcache-loop-1978.
kevin: If config change bottoms out, we'll shift ~30% traffic to na-west and enable dedicated overflow pool. Initiating gradual shift (10% every 5m) to avoid downstream overload.
ora: Started traffic-shift runbook step 1. Routing key `ap-south2->na-west` applied by router-v2.
ora: Router logs show successful weight changes: 10% -> 20% -> 30%. Latency on ap-south2 continuing to improve.
maria: After 30% shift + TTL bump, 95th at 210ms, 99th at 480ms. Still planning full rollback test of v1.9.6 in staging first.
sre-oncall: Keep monitoring for new evictions. If miss rate > baseline for next 30m, escalate to full rollback.
devon: Hotfix build passing tests. Will coordinate a canary restart of 3 nodes with patch `kvcache-fix-1.2.3` in 15m.
ops-bot: Note: scaling dedicated pool will allocate 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs in na-west. Estimated additional cost $3.2k/hr.
maria: Decision: accept config change + partial traffic shift + canary patch. Avoid full region failover unless metrics regress.
ora: Adding flamegraphs and heap stats capture for canary nodes. Command to collect: `kubectl exec -c runtime $POD -- sh -c \"curl -s http://127.0.0.1:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > /tmp/profile.pb\"`
kevin: After canary patch applied to 3 nodes, latency normalizes on canaries (95th ~110ms). Rolling patch across remaining nodes now.
maria: Rolling patch completed. ap-south2 95th stable at ~115ms, kvcache miss rate down to normal.
sre-oncall: INC-APAC-KVCACHE-1978123456 status -> mitigated. Postmortem to follow: collect rollout diff, metrics, and cost delta.
maria: Thanks team. Action items: (1) revert interim TTL/batcher tweaks after patch verified in 24h, (2) automated early-warning for KV miss storm, (3) evaluate if batching regression test needs to be added to CI.
kevin: I'll draft the postmortem and include cost numbers for the temporary capacity.
maria: Great. Closing comms channel for now, will reopen if regressions occur. :thumbsup:
